text:
lee-cust: Hey team — customer's production app started returning a ton of 429s around 11:00 UTC and a few duplicate completions are showing up in billing. They say traffic is bursty from a webhook fanout. Sample: they send ~200 concurrent completion requests after a DB event.

lee-cust: Here's a snippet of the client error we got back:

lee-cust: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2024 11:02:21 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 3
X-Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d
{
  \"error\": {\"message\": \"rate limit exceeded\", \"type\": \"rate_limit\"}
}
```

lee-cust: They said the SDK was retrying and they saw duplicates after a few retries succeeded. They aren't using Idempotency-Key right now. Can you advise on mitigating burst and whether this is an SDK bug?

alex-support: Ack, sorry you're seeing this — we'll triage. Quick questions:
- Can you paste the raw request headers (esp any X-Idempotency-Key / X-Request-ID)?
- What SDK + version?
- Are requests to the same model/route or different ones?

lee-cust: SDK is redwood-js v1.4.2, all requests are to /v1/completions (same model), no idempotency header. No custom retry config.

jamie-sdk: Thanks for the data. Quick context: redwood-js v1.4.x has a default retry policy of 3 retries with exponential backoff (base 400ms, factor 2, capped at 8s) + full jitter. For non-idempotent endpoints we recommended users set an Idempotency-Key; the SDK won't auto-generate one for create-style endpoints by default (we debated auto-gen but opted not to for safety).

jamie-sdk: If they're retrying without idempotency and a retry succeeds server-side after the original actually made progress, the application can end up with duplicate resources — which explains the billing/duplicate completions.

maria-oncall: From the infra side, this pattern smells like quota exhaustion + burst fanout. When the upstream sees many concurrent new sessions it returns 429 + Retry-After. The load spikes also sometimes fail-open to 503 if downstream resources are saturated. We need the X-RateLimit-* headers from those responses to confirm quota hit (Remaining, Limit, Reset).

lee-cust: I pulled a postmortem log snippet: server responded with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 in a few responses, Retry-After varied 2-4s. We also see a few 200s while others were 429s in the same second.

alex-support: OK that's consistent with quota exhaustion. Two parallel issues to fix: prevent duplicates (client-side idempotency + safe retry) and smooth the burst. Suggested quick mitigations:
- Add Idempotency-Key header per logical request (UUID) for create/completion calls.
- Increase SDK maxRetries from 3 -> 5 temporarily and tune backoff (add jitter if missing).
- Add client-side leaky-bucket or token-bucket to cap concurrency from that webhook worker (throttle at ~RPS target).

jamie-sdk: I'll add a docs blurb and a config snippet. Example code for redwood-js:

jamie-sdk: ```js
// recommended SDK config for bursts
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  maxRetries: 5,          // tolerate transient 429s
  backoffBaseMs: 300,     // start lower for shorter bursts
  backoffCapMs: 10000,    // don't back off forever
  jitter: 'full'          // spread retry timing
});

// ensure idempotency for creation-style endpoints
await client.completions.create({ prompt }, { headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': uuid() } });
```

jamie-sdk: Note: with Idempotency-Key, server will de-dupe based on the key for a configurable retention window; that'll stop duplicate billable resources.

maria-oncall: Additional infra mitigations (medium term):
- Implement per-customer token buckets at the edge so a sudden fanout is smoothed server-side.
- Track and surface sustained burst patterns in console (alert if 429 rate > 5% for > 5m).

lee-cust: Is there any risk changing maxRetries to 5 will make matters worse by increasing the total number of requests during a quota event?

alex-support: Good call. Yes, increasing retries without idempotency can increase load and worsen an overloaded headroom. That's why the order matters: first add idempotency, then adjust retries + client-side pacing. If you can't add idempotency right away, prefer client-side rate limiting over bumping retries.

jamie-sdk: Also: we discovered in a different thread that our default retry backoff had a bug in v1.4.2 where jitter wasn't applied to the first retry in some network error paths — that caused small bursts of aligned retries. We're preparing a patch. For now, ensure the SDK sets jitter:'full' explicitly in config or set a randomized delay on your webhook worker.

alex-support: Repro steps we asked the customer to try so we can root cause:
1) From a single worker, run:```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Idempotency-Key: test-$i" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/completions\" &
done
wait
```
2) Repeat without Idempotency-Key to see duplicate billing behavior.
3) Capture response headers (Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-Request-ID) and paste to thread.

lee-cust: We'll run that in staging and report back.

maria-oncall: Action items:
- jamie-sdk: follow up with a patch for v1.4.x to ensure jitter on first retry + consider an opt-in auto-idempotency flag for webhook-backed clients. (assigned)
- infra: add alert for sustained 429 spike and plan for edge token-bucket (tracked).
- support: follow up with customer with recommended SDK config + safe rollout plan.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: sdk-v1.4.3-patch to canary (cherry-pick jitter-fix) — started at 11:40 UTC :rocket:

alex-support: Thanks — marking this thread actionable. If customer can share X-Request-ID for a duplicate pair, we can correlate through logs and confirm if server created two resources or if client re-sent after success.

lee-cust: Got it. I'll send the headers once staging repro is done. Appreciate the triage 🙏

alex-support: No problem — ping us if they see anything unexpected while testing.
